subject.title: [Feature]: WebUI notification system, cron job management popups, and context monitor integration

question: What Control UI notification architecture and scope should OpenClaw own for cron completion actions, snooze/reschedule, and context-pressure prompts?
rationale: Current main already implements several adjacent pieces, but the remaining behavior requires choosing a shared UI event contract and deciding which cron/context prompts belong in core instead of ad hoc page-specific popups.

options.title: Scope a focused core design
options.body: Define the shared UI notification queue, cron-finished action model, and snooze/reschedule semantics before splitting implementation into smaller PRs.

options.title: Limit context to inline composer UI
options.body: Keep context pressure as the existing chat composer indicator and scope this issue only to cron/UI notifications and actions.

options.title: Defer to narrower trackers
options.body: Leave this broad issue as a tracker while narrower issues such as connected-session notify and webchat buttons advance independently.

recommendation.title: Scope a focused core design
recommendation.body: Define the shared UI notification queue, cron-finished action model, and snooze/reschedule semantics before splitting implementation into smaller PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent cron notification routing work is the closest maintainer-routing signal for deciding whether backend notifications should drive a shared Control UI queue.
